Definition: of Latin origin; a thousand paces, i.e. a "mile":--mile.
BiblicalUsage: The mile is the Roman thousand paces, and it appears once, in the Sermon on the Mount: if anyone compels you to go a mile, go with him two. The Roman soldier could lawfully press a man into carrying his pack for one mile, and Jesus doubles it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the second mile is the whole sermon in miniature: love does not stop at what is demanded, it goes further.
